<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
The irreducibility of the ${\mathfrak{g}}_0$-action on ${\mathfrak{g}}_{-1}$ implies both
statements.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Since ${\mathfrak{t}}'\subset{\mathfrak{u}}\subset{\mathfrak{w}}$ and ${\mathfrak{w}}$ is a~subalgebra, we have
$[{\mathfrak{t}}',{\mathfrak{w}}]\subset{\mathfrak{w}}$; as ${\mathfrak{t}}'$ acts on ${\mathfrak{g}}$ semi-simply, its invariant
subspace ${\mathfrak{w}}$ is the sum of its weight components. If ${\mathfrak{t}}\subset{\mathfrak{u}}$, then the
weight-$0$ component of ${\mathfrak{g}}$ is ${\mathfrak{t}}$ itself, and hence lies in ${\mathfrak{u}}$, whereas
the other weight spaces are the root spaces, of dimension $1$; therefore
a~${\mathfrak{w}}\supsetneq{\mathfrak{u}}$ contains a~whole root line ${\mathbb  C} x_\alpha$ with
$x_\alpha\not\in{\mathfrak{u}}$, and hence
${\mathfrak{w}}\supset\langle {\mathfrak{u}},x_\alpha\rangle={\mathfrak{g}}$.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
By conditions \eqref{cond3exc} and the symmetry $\alpha\mapsto-\alpha$ of the
root system, ${\mathfrak{g}}_1$ is an irreducible ${\mathfrak{g}}_0$-module and ${\mathfrak{g}}_1$ generates~${\mathfrak{g}}_+$. So $0\neq{\mathfrak{u}}_1\subseteq{\mathfrak{g}}_1$ forces ${\mathfrak{u}}_1={\mathfrak{g}}_1$, whence
${\mathfrak{u}}\supseteq{\mathfrak{g}}_-\oplus{\mathfrak{g}}_0\oplus{\mathfrak{g}}_+={\mathfrak{g}}$.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
1) The three modules ${\mathfrak{g}}_{\bar1}$ in the list \eqref{3excev} are
$2\boxtimes2\boxtimes2$, $2\boxtimes7$ and $2\boxtimes\spin_7$, all irreducible. If
${\mathfrak{u}}\supsetneq{\mathfrak{g}}_{\bar0}$, then ${\mathfrak{u}}$ contains a~non-zero odd element $x$, and hence
the ${\mathfrak{g}}_{\bar0}$-submodule generated by $x$, i.e., the whole of~${\mathfrak{g}}_{\bar1}$. 2) is
a~direct inspection of tables \eqref{tabOspGr}--\eqref{tabAbGr}: in a~contact grading
${\mathfrak{g}}_{-1}$ is purely odd and ${\mathfrak{g}}_{-2}$ is purely even.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
